newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall in quiet local trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall in quiet local trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.32 percent on Saturday in quiet trading by a few cautious local investors, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.49 points to 152.34 points in low turnover of 311,000 dinars ($439,000).
"There are still a few 1996 results coming out and people just have too little confidence to buy or sell at the moment," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments.
Brokers said they expected Saturday's subdued tone to carry through to Sunday, when the market will be open but many banks will be closed for Easter.

National Industries fell five percent on Saturday to 0.57 dinars, close to a 12-month low of 0.54, after announcing a 1996 loss of 1.07 million dinars, brokers said. That compared to a profit of 414,000 dinars in 1995.

But International Tobacco, which announced stronger than expected 1996 profits, rose 0.02 dinars to 1.18 dinars. Analyst Mohamed Abdallah of Pearl Consulting said its 1.86 million dinar profit compared with market expectations of around 1.5 million.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 19 to seven, with another 11 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.12 points to 81.03 points, 2.84 percent down from the start of the year.
